cost_settlement_gh454.verdict: THE AUTO-INVALIDATION CLAUSE FIRES. Billing-side single-wave cost is $0.959 - $1.022, i.e. ABOVE the charter constant $0.90 at BOTH ends of the bracket. The director's next trigger must re-rule the constant.
cost_settlement_gh454.why_this_wave_could_settle_it: GH #454 has been waiting since 2026-08-30 for a PURE SPOT WAVE THAT RUNS TO COMPLETION. W46 is it: market spot on all four, and all four SIRs closed `instance-terminated-by-user`, i.e. self-terminate with ZERO reclaims. W45 could not settle it (two of four reclaimed early).
cost_settlement_gh454.method: Same method §CO.5 used to set $0.90 on W29: per-machine runtime x the AZ's spot rate. NOT a bill line -- a true bill-line reconciliation needs a Cost Explorer read after the 4.3-11.3h lag band, which is not available this round and is NOT claimed here.
cost_settlement_gh454.runtime_bracket: Runtime is given as a BRACKET rather than a point because the EC2 records aged out (GH #375) and the only surviving timestamp is the SIR's Status.UpdateTime, which can lag the instance's actual stop. Lower bound = last S3 object -> definitely still running; upper bound = SIR close. Per machine the gap is 2m40s - 3m54s. Total machine-hours 3.385 (lower) .. 3.607 (upper).
cost_settlement_gh454.rates: c6i.4xlarge Linux/UNIX spot, describe-spot-price-history over the wave window, one row per AZ (no price change inside the window): us-west-2a $0.2959, us-west-2b $0.2740, us-west-2c $0.2967, us-west-2d $0.2474.
cost_settlement_gh454.total: EC2 spot $0.9422-$1.0037, plus public IPv4 at $0.005/h ($0.0169-$0.0180) = WAVE TOTAL $0.9591-$1.0217 vs the constant $0.90.
cost_settlement_gh454.robustness: The finding does not depend on where inside the bracket the truth sits: even the LOWER bound exceeds $0.90, and even EC2-only ($0.9422) exceeds it. To land under $0.90 the wave would have to have run ~22 minutes less in total than its own last S3 upload proves it ran.
cost_settlement_gh454.root_cause: PRICE, not runtime. Runtime 3.385-3.607 machine-hours brackets W29's clean 3.424, so the wave was the same size. The charter's spot band is quoted as $0.231-$0.250/h; THREE of the four AZs this wave priced ABOVE the top of that band ($0.2740, $0.2959, $0.2967), and the cheapest AZ ($0.2474) was already near its ceiling. The band, not the arithmetic, is what has gone stale.
cost_settlement_gh454.failure_direction: The stale constant under-records every spot wave in the fence arithmetic -- the DANGEROUS side, the same direction as the budgets MTD lag, and the two compound. This is the exact failure mode the constant's auto-invalidation clause was written to catch, and the clause worked: it is firing on the first wave that could test it, not on someone remembering to re-check.
cost_settlement_gh454.fence_impact: Small in absolute terms at today's cadence: ~$0.10-$0.12 per spot wave. September's fence reading is not changed materially (see the report). This is a re-rule-the-constant finding, not a brake-line event.

  (2) `seed 4209: needs survival_min, or both create and update` -> machines[] had `launched_at`/`terminated_at` but not the `create`/`update` names the tool reads.
Both are now filled from describe-spot-instance-requests and the gate reads RB_EXIT=0: `4 paired seed(s) of 4 machine(s) / 0 reclaimed before the flip / VERDICT: not blinded / NEXT WAVE: spot`.
WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE TWO FIELDS: GH #487 was filed last round on exactly one instance of this shape (null ab/ba), and last round's harvest_obligations named ab/ba ALONE. Had this round discharged only the obligation it was handed, the record would have read complete and honest, and the NEXT launching round would still have eaten an RB_EXIT=2 -- on two fields nobody had thought to name. The fix is therefore not a longer obligation list, which can only ever enumerate the failures already seen; it is that the round which WRITES the record is the round that must RUN the gate on it. An input-side gate whose input is written by a round that never executes it can only fail in the round that can least afford it. Handed to the director on GH #487.
